I cannot recommend this veterinary clinic highly enough. They have taken wonderful care of my cats over the years, and every visit has been a positive experience.

The receptionists are always warm, friendly, and welcoming. They are genuinely caring, helpful, and make both pets and owners feel comfortable from the moment you walk through the door.

The doctors are excellent—professional, knowledgeable, and compassionate. They take the time to thoroughly explain everything, answer questions, and ensure the best possible care for their patients. It is clear that they truly love animals and are dedicated to their wellbeing.

Kind regards from Walter and Joey x

In march I attended the vet as an emergency with my champion showdog who was having puppies and a puppy was stuck . The vet basically looked at her said yes the puppy was stuck and I asked for oxitocin to bring the puppy to which they said they didn’t have and she needed a C-section which they don’t do and I could take her to ucd or another vet . I asked is there nothing you can do for her to which they replied no so I put her back in my car and drove her to my vet over an hour away who was waiting and immediately after examination did a C-section and unfortunately the puppies were dead as such a delay getting down . My dog is perfectly fine tg . I have since got a bill of 65€ and 2 phone calls for basically not being able to do anything for my dog !  I will never attend this veterinary practice again .

I generally find them caring and helpful and the plan is excellent, I have all 3 of my dogs on it. The reception staff are very nice. The only negative thing I would say is they are eager to do unnecessary and costly tests sometimes and you have to be willing to stand your ground and say no or to push in order to get what you need. For example, my dog was recently diagnosed with arthritis but they won't give her the Labrella pain injection unless or until I get it confirmed via Xray, which would include a full anaesthetic and cost 500 quid. I just made an appointment somewhere else to get the pain shot for her instead. Arthritis is common, my dog is old and there are no symptoms indicative of any other acute injury so the x-rays are unnecessary in my opinion and it's not something I had to do for my other arthritic dog. So yeah, that's annoying but my experiences are mostly good.
